stages.title: 1. Extract the clinical story
stages.prompt: Which characteristic is most important to clarify?

options.text: Whether the sound is synchronous with the heartbeat and its onset/course

stages.feedback: Pulse synchrony is the defining feature highlighted in this case and changes the referral pathway.

stages.title: 2. Interpret the findings
stages.prompt: The case specifies a normal audiogram with a retrotympanic vascular anomaly. What does this suggest for reasoning?

options.text: A vascular/medical cause needs investigation rather than routine tinnitus management alone
The finding should be ignored if tinnitus is not loud

stages.feedback: The case is specifically designed to represent pulsatile tinnitus with a vascular red flag.

stages.title: 3. Check for red flags
stages.prompt: How should the presentation be classified within the learning workflow?

options.text: As a medical/vascular red flag requiring appropriate referral

stages.feedback: The supplied case explicitly states that pulsatile tinnitus requires vascular/medical referral.

stages.title: 4. Select management
stages.prompt: What should happen before routine tinnitus therapy is selected?

options.text: Arrange appropriate medical/ENT evaluation of the vascular finding
Start masking immediately and omit referral

stages.feedback: Medical evaluation takes priority in the specified vascular presentation.

stages.title: 5. Justify the decision
stages.prompt: Which reasoning statement best fits the case?

options.text: Pulse-synchronous tinnitus with a retrotympanic vascular finding warrants medical evaluation before routine tinnitus management
All tinnitus can be managed identically
A normal audiogram proves there is no relevant pathology

stages.feedback: The reasoning should connect tinnitus characteristics and the supplied finding to the referral decision without over-claiming a final diagnosis.

stages.title: 6. Plan follow-up

options.text: Document referral outcome and reassess hearing/tinnitus needs after medical evaluation
End follow-up regardless of medical findings

stages.feedback: Follow-up should incorporate the medical outcome and any continuing audiological needs.
